issues.t: 48V mild-hybrid electrical system fault warning
issues.sym: An "electrical system fault" message on the dash, start-stop that stops working, a weak or dead battery, and in rare cases a car that will not start.
issues.why: The 55 TFSI uses a 48-volt mild-hybrid system with a belt-driven starter-generator and its own battery. The starter-generator can fail, and Audi also found that faults on the data network (often from engine or brake-servo sensors) can make the starter-generator stop charging, which slowly drains the battery.
issues.next: Do not keep driving for long with this warning, because the car can lose power once the battery runs down. Have a dealer read the codes and check Audi bulletin 2073284 before replacing the starter-generator, since a sensor fault elsewhere may be the real cause.

issues.t: Water pump leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, a sweet smell after driving, crusty coolant residue near the front of the engine, or a low-coolant warning.
issues.why: The seal or bearing in the coolant pump on the supercharged 3.0 wears out. Owners commonly report failure around 50,000 to 60,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold and top up with the correct Audi coolant. If it keeps dropping, have the pump inspected soon. Pull over if the temperature gauge climbs.

issues.t: Thermostat sticks and causes overheating or slow warm-up
issues.sym: The temperature gauge runs high and the fans roar, or the engine takes a long time to warm up and the heater stays lukewarm. A check engine light with code P1B1C is common.
issues.why: The thermostat (which sits under the supercharger) can stick shut or open. Audi issued a bulletin for a thermostat defect on 2012-2013 cars, and the housing can also leak.
issues.next: If the gauge is in the red, stop and let the engine cool. Have the thermostat checked; many shops replace it together with the water pump and PCV valve since the supercharger must come off for all three.

issues.t: Torn PCV valve causes oil burning and whistling
issues.sym: Higher oil use, blue smoke at start-up, a whistle or hiss from under the engine cover, a rough idle, or a lean check engine code.
issues.why: The rubber diaphragm in the crankcase ventilation (PCV) valve tears, which upsets crankcase pressure and pulls oil into the intake. Audi has a bulletin tying extra oil use to this.
issues.next: Check the oil level often until it is fixed. Ask a shop to test crankcase pressure; the repair is labor-heavy because the supercharger has to be removed.

issues.t: Carbon buildup on intake valves causes rough running
issues.sym: Rough idle, stumbling or misfires on cold starts, harder starting, and power that slowly fades. A check engine light may come on.
issues.why: These are direct-injection engines, so fuel never washes the back of the intake valves. Oil vapor bakes onto them over time, especially with lots of short trips.
issues.next: Have misfire codes checked first (plugs and coils are simpler fixes). If carbon is confirmed, the valves are cleaned by walnut-shell blasting, usually around 60,000 to 80,000 miles.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle on cold start
issues.sym: A rattle from the engine for 1 to 3 seconds on the first start of the day. A rattle that gets longer or louder is a warning sign.
issues.why: One of the upper timing chain tensioners can lose oil pressure while the car sits. Audi issued a bulletin for 2011-2014 engines.
issues.next: Mention it to a shop and keep oil changes on time with Audi-approved oil. If the rattle grows, get it checked before a chain or guide fails; the chains are at the back of the engine, so the job is large.

issues.t: Supercharger whine or grinding from worn bearing
issues.sym: A whine or grinding noise that rises with engine speed, sometimes only on cold starts at first. Later you may feel less power.
issues.why: The front (nose cone) bearing of the supercharger wears from constant belt load, often after about 60,000 to 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the noise diagnosed early. If caught soon, the bearing can be replaced without replacing the whole supercharger.

issues.t: Oil pressure warning from a faulty pressure switch
issues.sym: A check engine light (code P164B) or an oil pressure warning, even though the oil level is fine.
issues.why: Audi found a defective oil pressure switch on 2011-2014 engines and released an updated part. On some 2013 cars, an oil filter that is too short sets a similar code.
issues.next: Any oil pressure warning is serious: stop and check the oil level first. If the level is fine, have a shop test real oil pressure and check the switch and filter before driving far.

issues.t: Rear spoiler error message or slow spoiler
issues.sym: A rear spoiler fault message, or the power spoiler moves slowly, jerks, or does not fully rise or lower.
issues.why: Corrosion in the spoiler drive hinges makes it stiff, so it cannot reach its end points (Audi bulletin for 2012-2016 A7). A weak 12V battery can also trigger spoiler faults on start-up.
issues.next: Have the battery tested first. If it is fine, a shop can clean and lubricate the spoiler hinges per Audi's bulletin, which is a short job.

issues.t: Diesel exhaust fluid (AdBlue) system faults
issues.sym: A warning about the AdBlue/diesel exhaust fluid system, often with a countdown to a no-restart condition.
issues.why: The pump or heater in the diesel exhaust fluid system that cleans the TDI's exhaust can fail.
issues.next: Do not ignore the countdown: the car may refuse to restart when it reaches zero. Have the DEF system diagnosed by a shop that knows Audi diesels.

issues.t: Coolant loss from pump or thermostat housing (55 TFSI)
issues.sym: A sweet coolant smell, coolant residue low on the engine, and a low-coolant warning.
issues.why: Coolant hoses, the thermostat housing and the coolant pump on the turbo V6 can seep. Audi has a bulletin on coolant loss from the pump on V6 TFSI engines.
issues.next: Check the level when cold and top up with Audi-approved coolant. If it keeps dropping, have the system pressure-tested before it overheats.

issues.t: Oil leaks around the engine (55 TFSI)
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, oil on the underbody or front end, or a burning oil smell.
issues.why: Audi released several bulletins on oil loss around the engine bay on its 3.0 and 2.9 TFSI engines.
issues.next: Have a shop locate the leak (Audi uses a UV dye test) and fix it, especially if oil can drip onto hot exhaust parts.

issues.t: Low coolant warning when the level is fine
issues.sym: The low-coolant light comes on even though the reservoir is at the right level.
issues.why: Audi issued repeated bulletins on diagnosing a low-coolant light with a normal coolant level, which points to the sensor or software rather than a leak.
issues.next: Check the level yourself with the engine cold. If it is correct, have a dealer check the sensor; if it is low, treat it as a real leak.

issues.t: Driver-assist and sensor warnings come and go
issues.sym: Lane assist, cruise control or collision warning switching off by themselves, plus random sensor error messages.
issues.why: Owners of early C8 A7s report many sensor and software faults; some were traced to the 48V starter-generator, others fixed with sensor repairs.
issues.next: Do not rely on driver aids while warnings show. Have a dealer read the fault history and check for software updates, which may be covered under warranty.

issues.t: MMI touchscreen freezes or reboots
issues.sym: The center screens freeze, go blank or blue, or restart while driving.
issues.why: Software faults in the MMI infotainment system, mostly on early cars, many of which were fixed by updates.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the latest MMI software update before replacing any hardware.

issues.t: Rear suspension clunk or rattle over bumps
issues.sym: A clunk, knock or rattle from the back of the car on rough roads.
issues.why: Audi has several bulletins for rear suspension clunking and rattling on these cars.
issues.next: Have the rear suspension checked to rule out loose or broken parts, then ask the dealer about the bulletin fix.

issues.t: Fuel can leak in the engine bay (recall)
issues.sym: A raw fuel smell, wet spots near the engine, or no warning at all.
issues.why: Several recalls cover fuel hoses, fuel line joints and injection parts that can weaken and leak (15V-019, 16V-646, 17V-781). Leaking fuel near a hot engine is a fire risk.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, do not drive the car; have it towed. Run your VIN for open recalls; the repair is free.

issues.t: Fuel rails can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell from the engine bay.
issues.why: Recall 19V-035: the left and right fuel rails on the supercharged V6 can leak fuel, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Stop driving and arrange a tow if you smell fuel. Check your VIN; the dealer replaces the rails free.

issues.t: Passenger airbag sensor can fail (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light, or the passenger airbag shows OFF when an adult is in the seat.
issues.why: The seat sensing mat that detects a passenger can wear out, so the passenger airbag may stay off in a crash (recalls 18V-370 and 15V-823).
issues.next: Have the recall done; until then, avoid seating an adult in front if the airbag shows OFF.

issues.t: Head curtain airbags may not deploy properly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptom.
issues.why: Recall 17V-293: the side curtain airbags may not inflate correctly in a crash.
issues.next: Run your VIN and book the free repair.

issues.t: Front airbags and belt tensioners may not work (recall)
issues.sym: Possibly an airbag warning light; often no symptom.
issues.why: Recall 16V-955: front and head airbags and seat belt pretensioners on some 2017 cars may not work properly.
issues.next: Check your VIN and get the free fix before carrying passengers.

issues.t: Auxiliary heater connector can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A hot or burning smell, or no symptom.
issues.why: Recall 18V-862: a connector for the auxiliary heater may not be fully inserted and can overheat.
issues.next: If you smell burning, stop and switch off the car. Check your VIN for the free repair.

issues.t: Backup camera image may not appear (recall)
issues.sym: A blank or frozen screen when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: Software and infotainment faults can stop the rear camera image from showing (recalls 25V-900, 22V-742 and 22V-806).
issues.next: Use your mirrors and look behind you. Have the free software or hardware recall fix done.

issues.t: Spilled drink in the back seat can shut the car down (recall)
issues.sym: After liquid is spilled in the rear, warning lights, loss of functions or a car that shuts down.
issues.why: Recall 22V-861: liquid in the rear seat area can reach and short the gateway control module.
issues.next: Keep drinks secure in the back. Get the free recall repair.

issues.t: Fuel gauge can stick and read wrong (recall)
issues.sym: The fuel gauge shows more fuel than is in the tank, and the car may run out unexpectedly.
issues.why: Recall 22V-155: the fuel level sender can stick.
issues.next: Track miles since your last fill-up until the recall is done, and refuel early.

issues.t: Rear suspension lock nut can break (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the rear, uneven tire wear, or the car pulling or feeling loose.
issues.why: Recall 21V-295: a lock nut on the rear trailing arm can crack from corrosion. A follow-up recall (22V-034) checks rear alignment after the earlier repair.
issues.next: If the rear feels loose or noisy, slow down and have it inspected. Get both recalls done free.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may not open properly (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom.
issues.why: Recalls 21V-159 and 20V-274: the tear seam in the dash over the passenger airbag may be formed wrong, so the bag may not deploy correctly.
issues.next: Check your VIN and book the free repair.

issues.t: Rear seat belt may not hold a child seat (recall)
issues.sym: A rear belt that does not stay locked when installing a child seat.
issues.why: Recall 21V-606: rear belt retractors can switch out of their child-seat locking mode too early.
issues.next: Install child seats with the LATCH anchors if possible, and get the free repair.

issues.t: Brake fluid cap may be mislabeled (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom; the wrong brake fluid may be added during service.
issues.why: Recall 23V-601: the cap on the brake fluid reservoir may list the wrong fluid type, which could lead to reduced braking.
issues.next: Have the recall done and make sure only the correct Audi brake fluid is used.

issues.t: Instrument display can go blank (recall)
issues.sym: The digital gauge cluster goes dark, so speed and warnings are not shown.
issues.why: Recall 25V-201: a software error can make the instrument display fail.
issues.next: If the display fails while driving, slow down carefully and use the head-up or center screen if available. Get the free software update.

issues.t: Lane departure warning can switch off (recall)
issues.sym: Lane departure warning stops working without warning.
issues.why: Recall 26V-125: a software error can turn off the lane departure warning.
issues.next: Do not rely on lane warnings until the free software update is done.
